standard_prerequisites.name: Envelope reduction setup: an envelope is a morphism g : Y' to Y as in Chow Homology, Definition chow-definition-envelope (canonical tag 0GU5)
standard_prerequisites.use: Since g is completely decomposed its pushforward on cycles is surjective, so verifying the identity for the base change by g settles it for D, i, E, j, X, Y, alpha.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of the Gysin map along a proper morphism: for f : X' to X proper and the pullback divisor square, if the invertible sheaf restricts trivially to D then i^* f_* alpha' = g_* (i')^* alpha' on cycles (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-closed-in-X-gysin, canonical tag 0H6D)
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the first and fifth equalities of the envelope chain of equalities.

standard_prerequisites.name: Push-pull formula for the cap action: in a cartesian square with g proper, f_*(g^*alpha cap beta') = alpha cap g_*beta' (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-action-push-pull, canonical tag 0H6B)
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the second and sixth equalities of the envelope chain of equalities.

standard_prerequisites.name: Locality of the cap action on open subschemes: (alpha cap beta)|_U = alpha|_U cap beta|_V for compatible opens (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-action-opens, canonical tag 0H67)
standard_prerequisites.use: With the evident locality of the Gysin maps, justifies replacing X and Y by open subschemes so the question may be assumed affine.

standard_prerequisites.name: Proper completely decomposed cover putting a relative cycle into the image of the cycle-classes map: for f : X to S finite type with S Noetherian there is a proper completely decomposed g : S' to S with g^*alpha in the image of the cycle-classes map (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-get-cycles, canonical tag 0H59)
standard_prerequisites.use: Together with the envelope paragraph reduces the quasi-compact case to alpha in the image of the cycle-classes construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cycle-classes construction: group homomorphism from the free abelian group on Hilb(X/S, r) to z(X/S, r) (relative-cycles chapter, Equation equation-cycle-classes, canonical tag 0H58)
standard_prerequisites.use: The image condition on alpha; by linearity the proof then reduces to a single class [Z/X/Y]_r.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cap product of a flat cycle class with a closed prime cycle: if Z is flat over Y of relative dimension at most r and W is closed of delta-dimension at most e, then [Z/X/Y]_r cap [W]_e = [Z x_Y W]_{r+e} (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-action-closed, canonical tag 0H6A)
standard_prerequisites.use: Used twice in the final computation to evaluate i^*alpha cap i^*[W] and j^*(alpha cap [W]) on the fibred products.

core_obligations: Prove that if L|_D is isomorphic to O_D then for every e the square formed by i^*alpha cap - and alpha cap - with the Gysin maps i^* and j^* commutes (proof lines 2636-2715). First, for an envelope g : Y' to Y (chow-definition-envelope, tag 0GU5) with base changes D', i', E', j', X', alpha' and projection f, run the six-step chain i^*alpha cap i^*g_*beta' = i^*alpha cap f_*(i')^*beta' = f_*(f^*i^*alpha cap (i')^*beta') = f_*((i')^*alpha' cap (i')^*beta') = f_*((j')^*(alpha' cap beta')) = j^*(f_*(f^*alpha cap beta')) = j^*(alpha cap g_*beta'), justifying the equalities successively by lemma-closed-in-X-gysin (tag 0H6D), lemma-action-push-pull (tag 0H6B), the definition of alpha', the induction hypothesis that the lemma holds for the base change, lemma-closed-in-X-gysin again, and lemma-action-push-pull again (proof lines 2637-2658); since g is completely decomposed the map g_* : Z_{e+1}(Y') to Z_{e+1}(Y) is surjective, so the identity holds for D, i, E, j, X, Y, alpha (proof lines 2667-2670). Second, fix beta in Z_{e+1}(Y); the desired equality (D to Y)^*alpha cap i^*beta = j^*(alpha cap beta) on E is local on E, and formation of the operators i^*, j^*, alpha cap - and (D to Y)^*alpha cap - commutes with localization (evident for the Gysin maps, and lemma-action-opens, tag 0H67, for the others), so X and Y may be replaced by open subschemes and assumed affine (proof lines 2672-2682). Third, for X and Y quasi-compact the envelope paragraph and lemma-get-cycles (tag 0H59) let one assume alpha in the image of equation-cycle-classes (tag 0H58); by linearity take alpha = [Z/X/Y]_r for a closed subscheme Z of X flat of relative dimension at most r over Y, and since beta is a finite combination of prime cycles, by linearity take beta = [W] for an integral closed subscheme W of delta-dimension e+1 (proof lines 2684-2694). Fourth, if W is contained in D then i^*[W] = 0 and alpha cap [W] is supported on E so j^*(alpha cap [W]) = 0 and the equality holds (proof lines 2696-2699). Fifth, if W is not contained in D then i^*[W] = [D cap W]_e and the pullback i^*alpha of [Z/X/Y]_r is [(E cap Z)/E/D]_r with E cap Z = E x_Y Z = D x_Y Z flat over D, so two applications of lemma-action-closed (tag 0H6A) give i^*alpha cap i^*[W] = [(E cap Z) x_D (D cap W)]_{r+e} = [E cap (Z x_Y W)]_{r+e} = j^*(alpha cap [W]) (proof lines 2701-2714).
proof_roadmap: Envelope reduction: prove the identity for a base change by an envelope through a six-step chain of equalities and conclude by surjectivity of the pushforward of a completely decomposed envelope (proof lines 2637-2670).
Localize on E and replace X and Y by open subschemes to assume them affine, using locality of the operators on opens (proof lines 2672-2682).

For quasi-compact X and Y put alpha into the image of the cycle-classes construction via the envelope paragraph and the proper cover lemma, then reduce by linearity to alpha = [Z/X/Y]_r and beta = [W] (proof lines 2684-2694).
Case W contained in D: both sides of the desired equality vanish (proof lines 2696-2699).
Case W not contained in D: compute both sides by two applications of the flat closed-pair cap formula on the fibred products (proof lines 2701-2714).
